name: HiFi SE Monoblock
description: Single-ended class-A monoblock power amp, fed from a line-level preamp. One small-signal driver into one triode-strapped output tube, ~8–12 W into 8 Ω. Sized for ~87 dB speakers (TriTrix MTM TL and modded Sony bookshelfs).

chassis.note: Standalone monoblock chassis — plenty of room, so octal and the bigger transmitting bases are all fair game. Compactron and duodecar excluded only because sockets are scarce.

heater_supply.note: Power transformer supplies 6.3 V; a second winding or buck-boost covers 12.6 V and 5 V rectifier rails.

output.opt: SE ~5k primary, 8 Ω secondary, gapped for ~60 mA DC (Edcor CXSE25-8-5K / Hammond 1628SE)

driver.label: Driver · voltage gain
driver.role: Single gain stage taking line level up to the output grid's swing requirement (~21 V RMS).
mu_bands: enough gain for line level in one stage
too low-µ to drive the output alone
driver.notes: Preamp already delivers about 1 V RMS, so roughly 25× gain covers full output. Frame-grid industrial types (E180F triode-strapped, EC8010, 5842/417A) are quiet and very linear here.

output.label: Output · SE class-A
output.role: Single-ended output tube, triode-strapped where it's a pentode/beam type.
output.notes: Triode-strapped SE gives roughly a third of plate dissipation as clean watts, so 20 W+ of dissipation is what gets you to 8–12 W output. That is the level ~87 dB speakers actually want.

rectifier.label: Rectifier · optional tube
rectifier.role: OPTIONAL — tube rectification for the softer, more dynamic supply behaviour. Solid-state is the tighter alternative.
rectifier.notes: 5Y3 sags most, 5AR4/GZ34 is stiffer and higher-current, EZ81 is the 9-pin option. Skip entirely and use UF4007s for the tightest bass.
